Thanks again for taking time yesterday — great to see the Cobalt team thinking through production runbooks. Attached is a concise proposal that lays out three reservation structures we commonly recommend for telemetry/embedding-heavy inference workloads: a Minimal Floor for cost-conscious pilots, a Stepped Ramp for predictable growth, and a Buffered Floor (with burst credits) if you expect spiky peaks. High level:

- Minimal Floor: 8 GPUs reserved, auto-burst to 12 for short windows, 30-day commit.
- Stepped Ramp: 16 -> 32 GPUs over 90 days (tranches at 30/60/90d).
- Buffered Floor: 24 GPUs reserved plus 12 GPU burst pool and 10% warm capacity; 6-month commit with a 30-day activation SLA.

Each option includes expected p95 latency targets, warm-start instructions, and a suggested monitoring playbook. I included an appendix with activation lead times and a sample ramp calendar so your procurement/infra teams can align internal budget and onboarding windows.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_options_v3.pdf (proposal), capacity-playbook-v2.pdf (ops runbook)

Hi Elena — quick technical follow-up on the minimum-floor / burst behavior so procurement has the specifics it needs: 

- Minimums and activation: Our serving pools can be configured with a 4 GPU warm floor that keeps model weights resident (suitable for low steady traffic). We can guarantee expansion from 4 -> 12 GPUs within 72 hours if the request profile is sustained; for faster sub-24-hour expansion we require a short warm-up credit (see billing note below).
- Burst credits mechanics: Burst credits are consumed when autoscaling exceeds the reserved pool and draws from the burst capacity. Credits are measured in GPU-hours; the proposal's Buffered Floor assumes a monthly pool of 360 GPU-hours (equivalent to 12 GPUs x 30 hours). Unused credits do NOT roll over; they reset at the start of the billing period. We can structure a capped rollover for enterprise accounts (negotiable).
- Pricing incentive at 60 days: From an infra standpoint we can align discounts to whichever tranche you prefer; operationally it's simpler to trigger a single larger discount at day 60 than smaller increments at 30/60/90. We'll reflect that in the revised term sheet.
- Warm-up / KV cache: For your embedding-heavy calls we recommend a 10% warm capacity to preserve p95 latency on cold starts; this is included in the Buffered Floor option.
- Activation lead times: On-prem/private deployments need 4-6 weeks, hosted Dedicated activation is typically 7-14 days for standard pools (subject to GPU availability) and 30 days for large (>64 GPU) bespoke pools.

Attachments: capacity-playbook-v2.pdf (ops details), cobalt-demo-logs-0310.txt (sample traces)

If it helps, Lauren can model three price scenarios (pilot, mid ramp, enterprise) and zip them into a one-page comparison for procurement.
